subject: Combinatorics

main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} For the uniform triangle-removal process starting from $K_n$, \[ \E\left[\left(\frac{F_n}{n^{3/2}}- \frac1{2\sqrt2}\right)^2\right]\longrightarrow0. \] In particular, \[ \frac{F_n}{n^{3/2}}\xrightarrow{\Prb}\frac1{2\sqrt2}, \qquad \frac{\E F_n}{n^{3/2}}\longrightarrow\frac1{2\sqrt2}. \] \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Delete uniformly random triangles from K_n until none remain. The number F_n of surviving edges satisfies F_n/n^{3/2} -> 1/(2 sqrt 2) ~ 0.3536 in L^2, hence in probability and in mean. This is the triangle case of Joos-Kuhn Conjecture 16.2 (which asks for convergence in probability).
main_statement.scope_note: introduction.tex:52-54: no claim for other starting graphs, general hypergraph removal, or fluctuations.

lean_comparator.verbatim: theorem sharp_terminal_leave : Tendsto (fun n => expectation n (fun G => (normalizedLeave n G - sharpConstant) ^ 2)) atTop (nhds 0) /\ (forall eps : R, 0 < eps -> Tendsto (fun n => probability n (fun G => eps < |normalizedLeave n G - sharpConstant|)) atTop (nhds 0)) /\ Tendsto (fun n => expectation n (fun G => (G.card : R)) / normalization n) atTop (nhds sharpConstant)
definitions_unfolded: Graph n := Finset (Finset (Fin n)); completeGraph n := all 2-subsets
triangles G := 3-subsets all of whose 2-subsets lie in G
step G := uniform triangle t of G, map to G \ (2-subsets of t); PMF.pure G if no triangle
evolve G k := k-fold bind of step; terminalLaw n := evolve (completeGraph n) (n.choose 2)
expectation, probability: finite sums against terminalLaw; normalization n := n^(3/2:R); sharpConstant := 1/(2*sqrt 2)

lean_comparator.match_check: Exact match with Thm main: all three conclusions (L2, in probability for every eps>0, normalized mean) are formalized. Running C(n,2) steps is enough because each removal deletes 3 edges and step is absorbing when triangle-free (Lean: Process/TerminalLaw.lean). Vertices are Fin n and graphs are Finsets of 2-sets rather than SimpleGraph, which is harmless.

D.max_item: E1 = I26 cluster (I23-I26: max-norm semigroup via star averaging); E2 = I40 cluster (I32-I40: o(1/D) collision bound); Lean-only L06 (self-contained prefix via moving-star stability) is the downstream use of E1.

evidence.quote: The continuation estimates developed here are the maximum-norm stability of the unfolding and the smaller than $D^{-1}$ error for adaptive paired queries.

caveats: Every ingredient of E1 (trace method, line-graph incidence identity, Dyson expansion) is individually classical; the N3 claim rests on the combination.
E2 is an elaborate estimate whose pieces (decreasing-path 1/l!, cycle-in-exploration certificates, template counts) have close precedents; it may fall to N2.
The constant itself is N0 (JK Conj 16.2; Spencer's branching law).

proof_architecture.claim: Prefix: run the process to density p = n^{-1/2+eps} (eps=1/2000); with prob 1-n^{-omega(1)} the graph has accurate degrees, codegrees, link-cycle counts (lengths <= 8000) and rooted-extension upper bounds. Paper: cite JK. Lean: own proof via Freedman + moving-star codegree stability + moment bounds (L06).
Continuation as a priority scan; edge survival decided by an exact recursive paired test with joint candidate ordering and full exposure.
Independent unfolding: fresh priorities per occurrence give exact product (cavity) identities for q_e, q_{e,T}, I_{e,T}.

Stability: in log-time s, z = log(q_e/q) satisfies z' = -(A/D)z + small; max-norm semigroup bound for e^{-sA/D} (link traces -> star approximation -> P = UV with VU = I+W -> mixed-norm Dyson expansion) closes a bootstrap: q_e = (1+o(1))(1+2Dt)^{-1/2} uniformly.
Coupling: finite vs independent root queries differ by at most P(some triangle type exposed twice); a repetition forces an extra-edge witness in the union of two visited ancestral call paths.

Witness count: embeddings of path unions with an extra edge carry D^{-B} (suffix template); visiting a prescribed pattern costs C_D^3 (2mu)^l/(h! l1! l2!) via off-pattern failures; summing gives O(D^{15-B}) = o(1/D).
Moments: one- and two-root probabilities give E[Y], E[Y^2] = 1+o(1) uniformly on good prefixes; m q(1)/n^{3/2} -> 1/(2sqrt2); bad prefixes cost Cn P(G^c) = o(1); L2, then Markov and Cauchy-Schwarz.

lean_route_differences: Prefix: the paper cites JK; Lean proves a triangle-specific prefix (UniformPrefixObligation, c=1/80000, polylog exponent 3*8001+2 instead of 2^{8002}-2) by Freedman-based tracking with the moving-star codegree stability (L04-L06). This is ~7k exclusive lines of the 21.9k-line target DAG.
Randomness: Lean uses discrete priorities in Fin N (grid) with explicit grid->continuum error lemmas instead of continuous uniforms (L02).

Unfolding: Lean defines the product-identity solution analytically by Picard iteration of a "cavity operator" in a BCF space (L03) instead of via an a.s.-finite random tree; the unfolding itself is an ExposureTree interpreted "fresh" (L01).

Collision bound: Lean's canonical_collision_sum has the form C^3 (3*prefixWeight)^l / l! (single factorial, constant 3) rather than the paper's (2mu)^l/(h! l1! l2!); the conclusion is the same o(1/D).

Semigroup: Lean reproduces ||exp(-sP)|| <= 1+2s exactly (graph_star_semigroup_bound) and the mixed-norm expansion abstractly over seminorms (MovingPerturbationFiniteExpansion.lean), reused for both continuation and prefix.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a line-by-line reading of all seven sections. Independently, the Lean library proves the comparator (identical to Thm main) from Mathlib alone, without the JK black box, with no sorry/axiom; this is strong (if the build is confirmed) evidence of correctness.
checked: Exact paired test (queries.tex:89-113): the iff claim and induction on priorities below threshold are correct; parent omission justified by strict threshold.
Product identities: candidate sets at f and g are disjoint after omitting T, and occurrence variables independent.
Exact z-equation: (dt/ds) q_e'/q_e + 1 with q_{f,T} = q_f/(1-I_{f,T}) reproduces eq. (exact-z); the constant term is 1 - d_e/D = O(n^{-c}).
E_0 formula: e^{-sUV} = Id - U int_0^s e^{-vVU} dv V verified by power series; ||e^{-v(I+W)}||_inf <= e^{-v}e^{v} = 1, so ||E_0||_inf <= 1+2s.
Dyson remainder: n (Cn^{-gamma})^K (log n)^K -> 0 needs K gamma > 1; paper takes > 2.
Bootstrap closure: needs a < c and a < 2 eps; stated (stability.tex:66-67, 356-358).
Short-pattern embedding: induced subgraphs of J have <= 2v-2 edges (root vertex orderings), so scaling >= D^v >= 1; count <= kappa (2m)^r D^l p.
Long-pattern suffix template: S(H,I) = D^L p = n^{-799/2000+o(1)} < 1 with all completion scalings <= 1; kappa <= (2D)^L D^{-B} since L > B.
Visitation bound: O_x necessary and conditionally independent; fork factor b(max)/(b(u)b(v)) = 1/b(min) <= C_D; at most two root steps; integrates to mu^j/j!.
Collision sum: 2 (patterns) x 2 (b-factor) x 2D (embedding) = 8D per step; sum of three exponentials = exp(24 D mu) = C_D^{12}; total C_D^{15} D^{-B}.
Moments: a_n = sqrt(D)/(2 sqrt(1+2D)) -> 1/(2sqrt2); (Y_n-1)^2 <= Cn and P(G^c) superpolynomially small.
Constant cross-check: JK Sec 16 heuristic with k=2, e(F)=v(F)=3, aut=6 gives p = (6/12)^{1/2} n^{-1/2} and R = n^2 p/2 = n^{3/2}/(2sqrt2).
